articles.title: California man found guilty of starting deadly and devastating Pacific Palisades fire
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — Almost five months after a first trial ended in a mistrial, a jury found a man guilty of starting what would become the devastating 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles that displaced thousands of people and became the most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles city history.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — Almost five months after a first trial ended in a mistrial, a jury found a man guilty of starting what would become the devastating 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles that displaced thousands of people and became the most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles city history. Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was convicted Friday on both federal counts against him: destruction of property by means of fire, and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. Sentencing was set for March 17. Rinderknecht faces a minimum of five years and a maximum of 40 years in prison, prosecutors said. The Palisades Fire, which began Jan. 7, 2025, was fueled by winds gusting up to 100 mph that fed on the very dry conditions. It killed 12 people, destroyed over 6,000 homes and other structures, and caused $25 billion in damage, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said. “The question at the time was who was responsible. And now we have the answer to that question,” Essayli said after the verdict. It was the second federal trial for Rinderknecht, who prosecutors alleged set a brush fire early New Year’s Day 2025 that was quickly contained by firefighters, but which continued to smolder and — seven days later — erupted into the Palisades Fire. “The strongest evidence was the defendant’s own testimony,” one of the jurors, who gave his name as Cameron and who said he initially voted to acquit, told reporters outside the courthouse after the verdict. The juror said Rinderknecht said that he was on the hill the night of the first fire, that he didn’t smell a fire or see fireworks and that it was a clear and calm night. “No one else was on the hill that day or night and happened to be smoking,” the juror said. “Everything kind of started to point to one conclusion — especially if there was no one else on that hill,” he said. Rinderknecht’s first trial in Los Angeles federal court ended in June with a mistrial after jurors deadlocked 10-2 in favor of an acquittal. His retrial began with jury selection on Nov. 2, and a panel comprising six men and six women began deliberating his fate on Wednesday. Prosecutors alleged that Rinderknecht, a former Los Angeles resident who was an Uber driver at the time, started the prelude to the Palisades Fire, a much smaller blaze known as the Lachman Fire. Named after a nearby street, this blaze was detected by environmental sensing platforms at 12:12 a.m. on Jan. 1, 2025, and was extinguished by firefighters after burning roughly five to eight acres of dense brush. But even though firefighters doused the flames, the “holdover fire” continued to smolder underground and was reignited a week later by the Santa Ana winds and grew into the monstrous Palisades Fire, prosecutors said. At the first trial, prosecutors painted Rinderknecht as a man mad at the world, citing passenger accounts of him ranting at them on New Year’s Eve. Rinderknecht “was angry all the time” and “believed he was enslaved by the wealthy,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Danbee Kim told the court. At the second trial, prosecutors seeking to convict Rinderknecht built a case against him using surveillance camera footage of his car driving in the Pacific Palisades neighborhood before the fire, GPS location information, and a green Bic barbecue lighter. “It’s not the traditional smoker’s lighter that I’m used to seeing,” LAPD Detective Matt Castellichio testified for the prosecution. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Williams said in closing arguments Wednesday that DNA from the lighter matched Rinderknecht’s DNA. The defense attorney, Steve Haney, said Rinderknecht admitted earlier to investigators he had the lighter with him. He said investigators found it in the glove compartment of his rental car, not at the scene of the Lachman Fire. After dropping off a passenger in the Palisades, Rinderknecht decided to walk up what’s known as Hidden Buddha Hill hoping to see some fireworks in the distance and ring in the new year, Haney said. After the environmental sensing platforms detected the Lachman Fire, Rinderknecht called 911 several times but his cellphone was out of service range. Those calls, Williams told the jury, were to create an alibi, and Rinderknecht had asked ChatGPT whether a person was at fault if a wildfire was caused by their cigarette. Rinderknecht also recorded images of the fire, Williams said. “The only verdict you can reach is guilty,” Williams said in his closing argument Wednesday. Haney said Rinderknecht should be acquitted because nobody saw him start the fire, no camera recorded the blaze being ignited, and that evidence at the site of the Lachman Fire had been compromised because the scene was open to the public for several days before it was closed by police. Ed Nordskog, a retired Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department arson and bomb investigator, testified earlier for the defense that “it appears hundreds of people visited the scene before it was locked down.” “In my experience, we call it a case killer,” Nordskog testified. The Palisades Fire burned 23,448 acres, resulted in 12 deaths and destroyed 6,837 homes, businesses and other structures, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department. Starting in the Santa Monica Mountains, it burned through the Pacific Palisades neighborhood and then spread rapidly through the Los Angeles County communities of Topanga and Malibu. It was more than three weeks before firefighters were able to corral the fire and the blaze wasn’t completely contained until Jan. 31, 2025. Los Angeles City Council member Traci Park, who represents the Palisades, said “there is no amount of courtroom justice that will ever undo the harm that was caused.” “What happened was just so deeply personal and traumatic,” she told NBC Los Angeles outside court Friday. The Los Angeles Fire Department on Friday thanked the jurors. “Our first thought remains with the families of those we lost and for everyone in our community whose lives were changed by this fire,” it said in a statement. “No verdict, however important, could ever undo that loss.” In the second trial, the juror who gave his name as Cameron said they initially took a vote, and he was the only one to vote not guilty. Ten others voted to convict and one was undecided, he said. “We sat there, and we just bounced our reasons why until we eventually met in the middle,” he said, adding: “We just continued and continued until eventually everyone did decide.” The juror said that the panel weighed the evidence carefully and knew that whatever they decided would have serious ramifications on Rinderknecht’s life. The juror wouldn’t say whether he believed Rinderknecht intended to burn down the Palisades. “His intent was to start a fire,” the juror said. “What that fire did after ... only he will know and God will know.” “The result of his fire is what ultimately led to January 7th,” the juror said.

articles.title: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime
articles.summary: EU warns COP31 risks turning into a ‘fossil summit’ as critical climate commitments are omitted from the draft deal.
articles.body:
The COP31 climate summit has gone into overtime as nearly 200 countries remain deadlocked over a draft deal that no longer mentions fossil fuels.

The two-week talks in Antalya, Turkiye, were due to end on Friday, when a late closing session approved some technical matters, but not the wider political deal.

“We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President and Turkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum told delegates.

Environmental groups tracking the two-week conference said the meeting lacked ambition to address the ‌worsening climate crisis and was on track to be the “worst COP ever”.

A third draft is expected on Saturday, the AFP news agency reported.

An opening draft from cohost and lead negotiator Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers objected.

Oil producers have also resisted similar language at past talks, including at COP28 in 2023. The revised text also dropped a $120bn target for money to help poorer countries adapt to climate change.

The European Union said the draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”. Panama, which signed a letter with a dozen other countries demanding “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”, threatened to walk away from the talks.

“It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover document that does not even mention fossil fuels, and we simply will not put up with it,” Panama’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, told a news conference.

The draft proposes raising the share of the world’s final energy consumption that comes from electricity to 35 percent by 2035. It does not say the power must come from renewables, and some countries want the target to say “clean”.

Some countries also reject a push to expand carbon capture, a technology that traps emissions from power plants and factories. They say it is costly and unproven, and could let polluters keep burning oil and gas.

“We want to see the references to false solutions removed,” said Vanuatu’s climate minister, Ralph Regenvanu.

Developing countries are angry that rich nations are falling short on climate finance. “We didn’t come here to beg,” said Ghana’s environment minister, Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings.

A UN report last month found the world is set to pass the 1.5-degree-Celsius (2.7F) warming limit set under the 2015 Paris Agreement.

The United States, the largest historical emitter, is absent for a second year after President Donald Trump ended climate cooperation.

The US-Israel war on Iran and higher living costs have also drawn attention away from the talks.

Environmental groups say the summit lacks ambition.

“This has been the worst COP ever,” said Mohamed Adow, director of the think tank Power Shift Africa.

articles.title: Verdict reached in Los Angeles retrial over 2025 Pacific Palisades wildfire that killed 12 people
articles.summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht was convicted of federal arson in the Pacific Palisades fire that killed 12 and destroyed nearly 7,000 homes after a mistrial.
articles.body: A man accused of sparking the deadly 2025 Pacific Palisades wildfire that killed 12 people and destroyed nearly 7,000 homes was found guilty on all counts Friday after a federal retrial in Los Angeles, months after his first trial ended in a mistrial. Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, a former Uber driver with dual U.S.-French citizenship, had been charged with two federal arson counts — including destruction of property by means of fire — in U.S. District Court. He was retried on a scaled-down grand jury indictment after his initial three-week trial ended in a hung jury in June. Ahead of the second trial, federal prosecutors dropped one of the original three charges against Rinderknecht, and modified the two remaining federal arson counts, reducing his maximum possible prison sentence from 45 years to 40 years. PALISADES FIRE SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY DRIVEN BY 'SOCIETAL REVENGE,' BEHAVIORAL ANALYST TESTIFIES IN COURT Following the verdict, a juror in the case — identified only by his first name, Cameron, who served as Juror No. 3 — told reporters that deliberations stretched across roughly two days as the panel systematically reviewed every piece of testimony and video evidence from the first day of court to the last. "I’ll be honest, I was the person who found him not guilty. Originally, I was the one who stood out on that. So it took a lot for me to be convinced otherwise," he said, noting the initial tally stood at 10 guilty, one not guilty and one undecided. Cameron said his initial hesitation centered on a "technical review" of the fire investigation and whether investigators properly followed protocol when linking the initial blaze to the later inferno. He said the jury ultimately concluded the defendant's own testimony — placing himself alone on the hill on a clear, calm night while smoking and carrying a lighter — pointed to him starting the first fire, which then smoldered into the Jan. 7 disaster. "What I will say is that his intent was to start a fire," Cameron said. "What that fire did after his actions, whether he can say or whether no one can say, like who knows? Only he will know and only God himself. And so the result of his fire is what ultimately led to January 7th [2025]." DEFENSE TEAM TRIES TO TIE NBA CHAMPION CHIS BOSH TO PALISADES ARSONIST CASE, CITING FIREWORK EVIDENCE: REPORT Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said in a statement following the conviction that "no verdict can bring back the lives lost or erase the pain families have endured." "Nearly two years ago, the Palisades Fire devastated our city, taking innocent lives, destroying thousands of homes, and changing so many lives and Los Angeles forever," Bass said. "So many are still struggling to rebuild. For those still displaced, the devastation remains a daily reality. "Los Angeles will always stand with Pacific Palisades." Los Angeles City Councilwoman Traci Park, who represents the Pacific Palisades, said the verdict "puts a bookend on one piece of this saga," though she emphasized that thousands of residents remain displaced and locked in disputes with insurance companies nearly two years later. "I don't think this takes heat off of the authorities," she said, pointing to breakdowns in infrastructure, evacuation routes, water systems and public safety staffing when the blaze rekindled. "And in my view, the real accountability comes in what we do next to prevent something like this from happening again." Prosecutors accused Rinderknecht of "maliciously" sparking a brush fire on Jan. 1, 2025 — initially dubbed the Lachman Fire — that was quickly extinguished, only to smolder underground in brush roots before strong winds fanned it into a massive inferno days later. articles.title: Sydney woman took her neighbours to court over three structures encroaching on her land, including a carport post crossing the boundary by just 3cm; the Supreme Court dismissed her case after the structures were removed
articles.summary: A Sydney woman took her neighbours to the Supreme Court of New South Wales over structures that extended onto her property, including a carport post that
articles.body: A Sydney woman took her neighbours to the Supreme Court of New South Wales over structures that extended onto her property, including a carport post that crossed the boundary by just 3 cm. The dispute involved adjoining homes in Lane Cove North and also covered a carport gutter and a garage eave and gutter, each found to encroach by about 13 cm.According to a judgment published by the Supreme Court of New South Wales, the neighbours accepted a boundary determination and agreed to remove the structures before the proceedings began. The work took longer than the woman wanted and involved several surveys and further repairs. The court later dismissed her summons and ordered each side to pay its own legal costs.Sydney woman discovered three carport and garage encroachments on her landThe structures had been in place since 1984. The dispute began after the woman engaged C&A Surveyors in June 2022 to survey the shared boundary before building a new dividing fence between the two neighbouring homes.The survey identified the encroachments and recommended a redefinition survey. The neighbours obtained their own survey in November 2023, which they said showed no encroachment. After correspondence between the parties, the woman applied for a formal boundary determination in August 2024.The Registrar-General issued the determination on 12 February 2025. It identified three encroachments: the neighbours’ garage eave and gutter extended approximately 13cm onto her land, the carport gutter crossed the boundary by about 13cm, and a carport post extended 3cm onto her property.Why did the carport and garage removal work take longer than expectedThe neighbours accepted the boundary determination and said they would remove the encroachments. In March 2025, the woman asked them to complete the work within 14 days. One neighbour replied that he was overseas and that removal would take place as soon as possible after his return.A plumber removed the carport gutter and downpipe in early April, but other work remained. The neighbour explained that roofing had to be removed and the buildings’ integrity considered.He said a licensed builder had been consulted and engaged, but the remaining work could not be completed until the end of May 2025 because of the builder’s workload and the woman’s request for a check survey. The remaining structures were not removed by then, and the neighbour later said he was waiting for contractors to become available in the area for the remaining repairs.Incorrect carport post work led to further proceedingsFinn Hawkins attended the property on 25 June 2025 to work on the carport posts but altered the wrong post. The woman began court proceedings in the Supreme Court on 7 July, seeking removal of the remaining structures as well as other orders concerning alleged trespass, entry onto her land and interference with survey marks.Those additional allegations were not adjudicated. Further work followed in September and October 2025 after the neighbours obtained another survey. That survey recorded no remaining encroachments, but the woman commissioned an independent inspection.A report in November identified some encroachments measuring between 1cm and 3cm. The neighbours arranged more work in March 2026 and again in May after a further inspection found one remaining encroachment.The court dismissed the case and ordered both sides to pay costsA joint inspection on 28 May 2026 was followed by a report confirming that the remaining encroaching structure had been removed.The substantive dispute was recorded as resolved on 17 July, leaving the question of legal costs for the court. The woman sought $56,649.37, including aggravated damages, or payment of her legal costs.The neighbours offered $20,000 in exchange for her discontinuing the proceedings, but neither offer was accepted.Justice Pike found that the neighbours had accepted the boundary determination and had consistently intended to remove the structures. articles.title: Philippines pet dumping: Dead dogs and cats were meant to be cremated - then their bodies appeared on a livestream
articles.summary: Grieving Filipinos confront a distressing reality: their dogs and cats may not have received the send-off they paid for.
articles.body:
A man – bald, goateed, wearing red-tinted sunglasses – walks down a cracked back road, guiding the camera towards a cluster of plastic-wrapped objects that spill out of the tall grass.

Names are written on the packages – Brandon; Ira; Lucky; Sweet – and numbers. One says 29kg (4.5 stone). Another says 2.5kg. Through the plastic you can make out what appears to be fur, claws and a flattened ear.

It's a mass dumping, the man explains. "We have about 25 animals here that have been dumped in bags. A couple of cats, some dogs."

Warning: This story contains images some might find upsetting

In the weeks since that video was streamed on Facebook, Chris and Geraldine Taylor, who run animal rescue NGO Luna and Furry Siblings (LAFS), say they have uncovered 15 dumping sites in the suburbs of Bulacan, near the Philippines' capital of Manila.

In total they've unearthed the remains of some 170 dead pets. Belgian Malinois, golden retrievers, pugs, puppies and cats have been found dumped off service roads, sealed in septic tanks, floating in rivers and buried in vacant lots.

Many of these animals are thought to have been sent to cremation businesses in the expectation they would be turned to ash.

Now, many grieving owners are having to confront a distressing reality: their beloved pets may not have received the send-off they paid for. The urn in their home may not contain their pet at all. And they may in fact see their so-called fur child again, jettisoned like common waste on the side of a highway.

One saw the livestream and wrote on Facebook: "I think one of those pets is mine." Below, they attached a photo of a beaming Alsatian.

When Chris arrived on that back road three weeks ago, he couldn't have known he was uncorking a scandal that would see at least one business reportedly shut, four people placed under investigation, and a personal invite to sit down with a senator to discuss animal-cruelty laws.

Chris, a former police officer, and his wife are retired, but only formally. For the past three years, they've been running an animal rescue shelter out of their home in San Jose del Monte, 30km (18.6 miles) north-east of central Manila.

On 30 October, he'd driven into town to report a case of animal neglect at the local district office. When he arrived, he was told the official in charge had just left to respond to another complaint: a report of dumped animals on a nearby roadside.

Chris had seen this once before: 14 dogs that were found and soon reburied. This time, he followed the official to the scene and started documenting – taking photos, scanning the bodies for microchips and uploading footage to his Facebook page.

"I figured there's got to be more to this," he explains. "So we put out word: if anybody knows anything, any other dump locations... just report it. Let us know."

In the days that followed, tip-offs started trickling in. More dumpsites emerged.

"The long vacant lot on the left side... that's where the smell comes from," read one message.

"When we ran to this place it smelled of rotting animals," read another, accompanied by a photo of a map with a location circled in red.

By crowdsourcing intel in this way, and collaborating with authorities, LAFS has so far uncovered a total of 15 dumpsites, containing an estimated 170 animals. "Some of them were just bags of bones," Chris says. "Others were liquefied."

LAFS has meticulously documented the crime scenes. Often wearing little more for protection than an N95 mask and rubber gloves, Chris crouches in the underbrush and slices open discarded plastic bags, picking through the contents while Geraldine holds the camera.

Their Facebook videos have racked up more than 30 million views. Commenters ask Chris if he has seen their pet among the bodies, or if he can turn a carcass over so they can check for identifying marks.

Some are successful. On that first night in October, all 25 bodies were returned to their owners.

There's a question which hangs uncomfortably over every dumpsite: who would do something like this?

As more owners came forward, a common denominator emerged. Many said they'd taken the animals to be incinerated at the same place: a crematorium called Ahjay Paws in the city of Bacoor, not far from Manila.

"So I posted: anybody that's had Ahjay's services... these might be your animals," says Chris. "And man, it just flooded in."

The Philippines has long been a dog-loving nation, but since the Covid-19 pandemic the "fur parenting" community has exploded.

A 2021 study found the country had the highest rate of dog ownership in the Asia-Pacific. Since then, the pet dog population has increased 4.7% year on year, according to another study, exceeding 21 million in 2025.

As the numbers soar, businesses have stepped up to address an inevitable implication: more deaths.

"Cremation here in the Philippines has become quite a big thing with the boom of the pet industry," says Anna Cabrera, director at the Philippine Animal Welfare Society (Paws). "There's even a ceremony where they hold wakes for the pets."

These events offer grieving owners a last chance to see their beloved pets before they're taken to a crematorium and transmuted into an urnful of ashes.

Revecca Calling, who lives south of Bulacan in the city of Cavite, says she paid Ahjay Paws 8,500 Philippine pesos (£100; $133) to cremate her dog Olaf in January. The price was calculated according to weight, and included a 30-minute viewing where she could say her final goodbye.

Calling says Ahjay Paws told her they couldn't record the cremation, as it might endanger the staff. They took away Olaf's body, and a few days later handed back a small urn that purportedly contained her cremated remains.

When nine months later Calling heard that dozens of animals' bodies had been found dumped on an empty plot of land, potentially at the behest of a pet cremation business, she was devastated.

"Pet owners entrust these services with something very important: the remains of a beloved family member," she says. "We need to know what happened."

Earlier this month, the Philippines' National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) filed criminal complaints against four individuals in connection with dumped pets. Among them is the owner of Ahjay Paws and two people who ran Bulacan's Pet HPHT Crematory.

According to the NBI, Ahjay Paws had initially arranged to acquire a cremation machine from Pet HPHT – but when it didn't arrive, they opted to send the pet remains to Pet HPHT instead. When the volume of those remains became more than Pet HPHT could handle, that firm paid a third party to bury them.

One interpretation is that the dumping incidents are a result of logistical failures: two businesses that bit off more than they could chew and took desperate measures to make the problem go away.

But there's another theory: that the dead pets could be evidence of a lucrative racket, with people's money taken to incinerate their pets but the animals then being dumped instead.

There is a word for this kind of deception in Philippine law – estafa; where a perpetrator knowingly misleads a victim to financially defraud them – and the NBI say they are investigating it as a possibility in this case.

Two weeks ago, Ahjay Paws' owner denied responsibility for the dumping in San Jose del Monte, according to local media. The company is apparently no longer operating, and the BBC has been unable to contact it.

The BBC has also reached out to Pet HPHT and invited it to respond. On Facebook, the firm said the dumping allegations were "completely false and have no basis".

Another grieving pet owner, Emelia Legada, says she paid Ahjay Paws 10,000 Philippine pesos (£120; $160) to cremate her dog Harvey six months ago.

"I just can't accept the pain of not knowing what might have happened to him," she says. "I really want to confirm whether Harvey was properly cremated, and whether the ashes I received were truly his."

Many are wrestling with the same uncertainty. As Cabrera puts it: "God knows what that was inside those urns."

In response to those anxieties, a veterinarian in nearby Quezon City has started offering complimentary forensic ash testing. For those whose pets have been found among the bodies, other crematoriums have offered to do the job properly, and for free.

The animal welfare society, Paws, is volunteering legal services to help people file complaints with the authorities, and has received more than 150 requests so far. It is also calling for a nationwide audit of all pet cremation businesses.

On 2 November, Percival Vilar Cendaña of the Philippines' progressive Akbayan Party appeared on national television. He was there to speak about the pet-dumping scandal, which, in the span of a few days, had flared into a national disgrace.

"Our worst fears have been confirmed," he told the Bilyonaryo news channel. "Now we see that these are not isolated incidents. It is true that this is a syndicate that is conducting widespread operations."

Neither the police nor the NBI have confirmed that the dumpings were carried out by a "syndicate", nor that they were "widespread". Many details surrounding the case remain murky. But the hysteria is real – and Cendaña was giving voice to a common sentiment.

"Those who deceived these poor fur parents should be jailed," he said.

At least three individuals have surrendered to the NBI and been charged with violating the city's Code of Sanitation, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, and the Sanitation Code of the Philippines.

But many feel this doesn't go far enough, and say it fails to hold anyone liable for the way the animals' remains were treated.

Cabrera says the country's animal-cruelty law doesn't cover the treatment of animals after death. And "there's no crime if there's no law".

The scandal has prompted a groundswell to change that. Lawmakers like Cendaña are pushing for a national commission on animal welfare to ensure their dignity in life and death.

Meanwhile, Cabrera says Paws will seek "moral and exemplary" damages on behalf of aggrieved pet owners.

One woman whose dog was suspected to have been found among the dumped bodies told the BBC she couldn't speak about it because she was "feeling weak".

"I haven't slept for three days from all the crying," she said.

Chris has also been losing sleep, taking calls from grieving pet owners who have watched his videos. "Hundreds of people call me in tears, just sobbing," he says.

"They're in so much pain. And half the time you're telling them: 'you're not going to find your pet. It's been too long; we're not going to be able to identify it.' And it just crushes them."

As well as new laws, Chris wants stricter enforcement of existing rules. He wants to know how he managed to unearth so much in the space of a fortnight, and why people keep coming to him saying they don't trust the police to take their concerns seriously, he says.

The BBC contacted Philippine National Police (PNP) for comment, but didn't hear back. Earlier this month, PNP chief Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr said authorities were determined to hold accountable those who allegedly took advantage of grieving pet owners, saying such exploitation "must be addressed with the full force of the law", according to ABS-CBN.

"Fraud is not measured solely by the amount of money taken, but also by the damage inflicted on the people whose trust has been betrayed," Nartatez said.

"To the affected pet owners, we recognise the pain and distress this incident has caused your families."

Yet the police themselves have come under official scrutiny.

On Monday, the National Police Commission announced an investigation into officers in Cavite and Bulacan after they suggested LAFS might be involved in the pet dumping because they were often first on the scene. The officers did not present evidence for their claims. The investigation also covers reports that officers visited the Taylors' home and took photographs.

Meanwhile, countless grieving pet owners are suspended in purgatory: desperate for closure on what happened to their dogs and cats, and calling on authorities to do more.

"We want the case to be properly investigated and those responsible to be held accountable," says Calling. "I believe that no secret remains hidden forever."

Legada, for her part, says: "I just want to find out what really happened to Harvey and where his remains are. I want to know whether he was properly cremated."

She also wants people to know: "You can't trust anyone these days."

With additional reporting by Virma Simonette Rivera

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to meet India PM Modi on first trip abroad
articles.summary: Trade, connectivity and regional cooperation will be on top of the agenda when Nepal's PM meets his India counterpart.
articles.body:
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah's visit to India has raised hopes of a reset, marking the first high-level engagement between leaders of Nepal's new political generation and its giant neighbour.

It is Shah's first bilateral visit since his Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) swept to power in March, six months after a Gen Z uprising against corruption and nepotism toppled K P Sharma Oli's government.

The 36-year-old rapper-turned-politician arrives in Delhi on Sunday for a two-day visit, during which he will meet his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi and other senior officials.

The talks are expected to cover a broad range of issues, including economic and energy cooperation, the opening of new air corridors, and a reconstruction assistance package following the devastating flash floods that struck Nepal in August.

The disaster killed more than 1,450 in the Himalayan nation, while thousands remain missing and unaccounted for.

India and Nepal share close ethnic, cultural, religious and economic ties, with a largely open border stretching more than 1,750km (1,080 miles).

Wedged between India and China, Nepal is a strategic buffer and, analysts say, its stability has direct implications for India's security.

But over the decades the relationship has been strained by territorial disputes, allegations of political interference and resentment over what many in Nepal see as the dominant 'Big Brother' attitude of Delhi.

Nevertheless, analysts see Shah's visit as an opportunity for a reset.

"The new Nepali leadership says they do not have the political baggage of the past and they want to focus on development, diplomacy and economic partnership," Ranjit Rae, a former Indian ambassador to Nepal tells BBC.

"They seem to be more pragmatic, less ideological. I personally feel it's an optimistic moment," he adds.

Since Nepal abolished monarchy and became a democratic republic in 2008 three political parties dominated the governance.

Delhi has maintained close contacts with all of them – the Communist Party of Nepal (CPN – UML), the Nepali Congress and the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist Centre).

Nepal's communist parties were seen as closer to India's rival China, owing to ideological ties, and often criticised Delhi over what they viewed as unequal bilateral agreements.

Due to Nepal's strategic location, both Delhi and Beijing compete for influence in Kathmandu, leading to accusations the two Asian giants are meddling in the internal affairs of Nepal.

But Nepal's ties with India extend beyond diplomacy and strategic interests.

The Hindu-majority nations share deep social ties, with families straddling the open border and communities interacting daily.

Bilateral trade exceeds $9bn, heavily skewed in India's favour - a longstanding source of resentment in Kathmandu. India is also Nepal's main supplier of petroleum products and several food items, and a key transit route for its trade with the rest of the world.

One key area of co-operation is hydropower. India has approved projects to import up to 1,200MW of electricity from Nepal and is looking to expand imports further.

"India has a huge demand for electricity and Nepal has the potential to generate due to its water resources and geography. It's not just bilateral, Nepal also exports electricity to Bangladesh via India," says Rae.

India has often been among the first countries to assist Nepal during major natural disasters, including the 2015 earthquake and the flash floods in August this year.

Despite the close links, Nepal and India have their differences.

In 2019, Nepal was furious after India published a map that included areas claimed by Kathmandu, in a western region close to the border with China, as part of its territory. That raised heightened awareness in Kathmandu about the region.

The diplomatic wrangle escalated after Nepal published its own map which included those disputed areas.

"I hope Nepal's prime minister raises the border issue with Delhi this time. There may not be a resolution immediately, but they should start negotiations to settle the issue," Kanak Mani Dixit, a veteran Nepali political analyst, told the BBC.

Nepal has also long urged India to open additional air entry routes, allowing large aircraft to fly in from the west to its new airports at Bhairahawa, near the Buddhist holy site of Lumbini, and Pokhara, a major tourist destination.

Access to Indian airspace would mean shorter flights at lower cost and, with more flights, the airports would become commercially viable.

Some in Nepal also believe that Delhi is wary of the fact that the Gautam Buddha international airport was constructed by China's Northwest Civil Aviation Airport and the airport in Pokhara was built with Chinese financial assistance .

Shah has yet to make any overtures to Beijing, but sent a 20-member delegation of party MPs to China for an 11-day visit from 15 November, ahead of his trip to India - seen as an effort to balance ties with Nepal's two powerful neighbours.

Shah had pledged not to travel abroad during his first year in office, but devastating flash floods in August have changed the calculus.

His government estimates reconstruction will cost nearly $5bn, while international aid pledged so far has fallen short of expectations.

But some observers in Nepal believe that Shah's preparations for the high-stake India visit have been less than thorough.

"Prime Minister Shah and his advisors are young and fresh, but they do lack experience. Repeatedly they have exhibited a lack of gravitas in governance, which would be essential for diplomacy with an overwhelmingly powerful neighbour," says Dixit.

Shah is already facing criticism over some of his government's recent decisions, including to remove police chief Dan Bahadur from his post after he allegedly refused to comply with directives from the Prime Minister's office.

Police were sent to some news organisations to detain journalists for their news coverage triggering accusations of curtailing press freedom.

While Kathmandu has ambitions in advancing its ties with India, the real test for Shah would be to return home with tangible outcomes. Securing concrete commitments from Delhi on financial aid would be seen as a diplomatic success and could help blunt growing domestic criticism.

articles.title: Jawan hit by own gun, friendly fire during op to get war pension: SC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: It is not necessary for Army personnel to be hit by an enemy's bullet in order to be entitled to pension under War Injury Element, Supreme
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It is not necessary for Army personnel to be hit by an enemy's bullet in order to be entitled to pension under War Injury Element, Supreme Court ruled Friday, ordering that pension be granted even in a case where a soldier is injured in accidental firing from his own gun or his own troops during an operation.A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N K Singh said that the order specifically mentioned that Army personnel would be classified as 'Wounded Battle Casualty' in such cases and the grievously injured soldier would be entitled to the pension.The court said the Army order contemplated two situations: a gunshot or splinter injury suffered 'accidentally', or such an injury caused by firing by own troops. "In either situation, the injury must have been sustained while carrying out operations against the enemy or militants. The present case rests on the first limb, 'sustained accidentally'," SC said."A service weapon may discharge without an intention to cause bodily injury to himself, for example, while holding a weapon, an impact or fall, snagging of the trigger, inadvertent pressure on the trigger, or a mechanical defect... These nature of incidents are clearly distinguishable from the idea of self-inflicted injury, which has a certain element of knowledge or intention so as to disqualify from getting enhanced pensionary benefit," the bench said.SC allowed the plea of Subedar Major and Honorary Lieutenant Devi Singh who got injured in Aug 2002 during Operation Rakshak/Operation Parakram in J&K when his weapon accidentally discharged a bullet that passed through his thigh and damaged the femoral vein. It made him 40% disabled and he was granted an ordinary Disability Element of pension. He sought an enhanced pension under War Injury Element. SC quashed the order of Armed Forces Tribunal, which had rejected his claim.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'The View' co-host stunned as Hostin backs Gavin Newsom bypassing victims' families for death row commutations
articles.summary: Sunny Hostin and Ana Navarro were split over Newsom's 548 death row commutations, and Navarro argued that Gov. Gavin Newsom should have notified the families.
articles.body: "The View" co-host Ana Navarro appeared surprised when co-host Sunny Hostin disagreed with her argument that Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom should have notified the victims' families before ending the death sentences of 548 inmates in his state. "I don’t like the way it went through. And I think that before he announced that, he needed to get the approval and agreement of the families of the victims, because the people that he’s commuted the sentences for are people who are on death row. They’re people who committed murder, and I tend to be against blanket pardon to begin with," Navarro said. Newsom commuted the death sentences of all of California's death-row inmates in early November, effectively ending capital punishment in the state years after issuing an executive moratorium on executions. CALIFORNIA PROSECUTORS SLAM NEWSOM'S DEATH ROW COMMUTATIONS, ACCUSE GOVERNOR OF PUTTING 'POLITICS OVER PEOPLE' "I think these are things you have to take on a case-by-case basis, and I think it’s disrespectful to the victims’ families," Navarro said. "You can disagree or agree with the death penalty, but to me, if your loved one has been murdered, you have the right to be told that this is happening, before you read about it." Hostin said, "I disagree with that." "That the victim's family should have been told?" Navarro asked in response. "Yes," Hostin repeated. "I'm an opponent of the death penalty. I think that God gives life." Hostin said those cases were under Newsom's purview as governor. She argued that the system is "broken," and no one should have to pay the ultimate price for a broken system. ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION "One innocent person being put to death is not worth the entire system," she said. "And if you look at the system, it's not a deterrent. That the statistics show that more than half of death row exonerees are Black, even though Black people just make up 13.6% of the U.S. population. "And nearly 60% of the people that are found to have been wrongfully convicted of murder by the Innocence Project are African Americans, and so the system is broken," Hostin continued. "And you should not pay the ultimate price for a system that is broken." Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin sided with Navarro, arguing the move was a betrayal of the families. "It was a betrayal of the families to not notify them beforehand," Griffin said. "People can agree or disagree on the death penalty. It's actually come up as a ballot initiative in California twice in the last decade. And California voters actually voted to keep capital punishment in place. "I think (Newsom) has the purview to do this, but then to not notify families, that gets in the way of their grief," she added. "There's no greater trauma than having a loved one murdered in a brutal way and thinking it's been adjudicated in the court, and there's a certain outcome in finding out in a newspaper, basically, that that's not happening." GAVIN NEWSOM SEEKS COUNSEL FROM ‘MASTER’ BILL CLINTON AS HE PLOTS PROJECT 2029 Griffin also said it could be a political move by Newsom. "This should have been handled better," she said. "And I think there's a political side to this too. He wants to run for president. He wants to seem more progressive. Kamala Harris may run for president. He's gonna be like, ‘She was a prosecutor who put people in jail.’ So, I don't like it. He should have notified the families." Co-host Sara Haines agreed, arguing that undoing all the death sentences treated each case the same. "I think the point is that if you want to change something going forward, put it on a ballot, and clearly California doesn't want it taken off," she said. "At that point, I think he should have looked case-by-case, because to not reach out to these families, they get nothing back. "Any closure they get is small. But some of these people deeply found something in this conviction and this determination. And to just undo it in one blanket swipe is to treat them all the same." When reached for comment, the governor's office referred Fox News Digital to a letter Newsom issued explaining his decision. In part, Newsom wrote, "This decision is among the most difficult of my career, not because I doubt its necessity for our state but because I know its announcement may surface excruciating memories for victims' families. I deeply respect the views of those who will strongly disagree with my decision, including some families of victims who have suffered the worst possible loss. "I hold this painful truth along with the belief that this is a righteous action," he continued. "Today I am acting on my long and deeply held conviction that individually and collectively we are stronger as a society when we reject state-sanctioned killing." Later in the letter, Newsom said, "California voters have voted to keep the death penalty on the books, and I respect that. I recognize the limits of this clemency action, which does not repeal the death penalty and is limited to commuting California's current death sentences. The power to repeal the death penalty rests with the Legislature and voters." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "Victims’ rights were disregarded and trampled by Governor Newsom," Y. David Scharf, chairman of Morrison Cohen LLP, told Fox News Digital in a statement. "Whatever one’s view of the death penalty, the families of murder victims deserved more than to learn that the sentences in their loved ones’ cases were being swept away as part of a blanket decision affecting hundreds of cases. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The governor may have the constitutional authority to commute these sentences, but having the power to do something does not mean the people most profoundly affected by it should be treated as an afterthought," he continued. "At a minimum, these families deserved notice, respect and an opportunity to be heard before such a consequential decision was announced."

articles.title: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria
articles.summary: Police say two children among dead as search continues for more victims.
articles.body:
A boat believed to be carrying hundreds of people to a funeral has overturned in southern Nigeria, killing at least four people, according to police.

The overcrowded vessel capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure while travelling from the communities of Ayama to Ukubie, police spokesperson Musa Mohammed told the Reuters news agency.

He said the dead were two adults and two children.

Police said 24 people were rescued, with 19 treated at a local clinic, and five taken to a hospital in the state capital.

Search teams were still looking for more victims, police said. Police did not say how many people were on board, but some residents told Reuters there were at least 300.

Police said the driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.

According to a statement from the Bayelsa State Police Command, the accident occurred at the river junction between the Oweikorogha and Otuan communities, in the state’s Southern Ijaw district.

The boat that capsized was travelling “for a burial ceremony”, the statement also said, adding that police are “coordinating efforts with local divers and other responders”.

Such boat accidents are common on Nigeria’s busy rivers and waterways, often caused by overloaded vessels, poor maintenance or failure to comply with safety regulations.

A similar incident occurred in August, when at least 51 died after a boat sank in northwest Nigeria’s Sokoto State , and another in January, when at least 26 people drowned after a boat ferrying people from Jigawa to Yobe State capsized.

articles.title: Ex-procurador-geral do Paraguai denuncia perseguição política à ONU após escândalo bancário | G1
articles.standfirst: Emiliano Rolón é acusado de dificultar investigações sobre o Ueno Bank; Ministério Público abriu investigação contra ele nesta sexta (20)
articles.summary: Emiliano Rolón é acusado de dificultar investigações sobre o Ueno Bank; Ministério Público abriu investigação contra ele nesta sexta (20)
articles.body:
Procurador-geral do Paraguai Emiliano Rolón Fernández — Foto: AFP / Procuradoria-Geral do Paraguai

O ex-procurador-geral do Paraguai Emiliano Rolón denunciou à ONU uma perseguição política após renunciar ao cargo em meio ao escândalo envolvendo o Ueno Bank , que levou à destituição e à prisão do ex-presidente Santiago Peña, segundo documentos obtidos nesta sexta-feira (20) pela AFP.

Rolón renunciou na terça-feira (17), enquanto deputados articulavam um pedido de impeachment contra ele. Dois dias depois, a deputada Rocío Vallejo e a senadora Yolanda Paredes, ambas da oposição, apresentaram uma denúncia criminal contra o ex-procurador por suposta obstrução da persecução penal, tráfico de influência e associação criminosa, de acordo com documentos divulgados no X.

As parlamentares o acusam de dificultar as investigações sobre o Ueno Bank e de atrasar buscas e apreensões em empresas ligadas ao banco e ao grupo financeiro . Com base nessa denúncia, o Ministério Público abriu nesta sexta-feira uma investigação criminal contra Rolón.

O Banco Central do Paraguai interveio no Ueno Bank em 3 de novembro devido a graves problemas de solvência, deixando temporariamente centenas de milhares de clientes sem acesso aos seus depósitos. O agora ex-presidente Peña é acusado de favorecer a instituição financeira, com a qual mantinha vínculos empresariais.

Nesta sexta-feira, Rolón apresentou um documento à relatoria das Nações Unidas responsável pela independência de juízes e advogados, no qual denunciou uma “perseguição penal com motivação política e midiática” contra ele, segundo o texto ao qual a AFP teve acesso.

Ele argumenta que a investigação sobre o banco provocou “reações de diversos setores, entre eles parlamentares e meios de comunicação, principalmente, hostilizando a atividade investigativa”.

Rolón anexou ainda uma manifestação de defesa na qual critica o uso de denúncias e processos criminais “como ferramenta de pressão, desgaste ou represália contra juízes e promotores em razão do teor ou do ritmo de suas atuações funcionais”.

Após sua renúncia, a promotora Alba Rocío Cantero assumiu a chefia do Ministério Público paraguaio.

articles.title: g1 Zona da Mata: Morte em canal e gêmeos do Vou Zuar presos | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira quais foram as notícias em destaque no g1 Zona da Mata entre 14 e 20 de novembro.
articles.summary: Notícias da Zona da Mata destacam a investigação de morte em dentista, a prisão de integrantes do grupo Vou Zuar e o ouro internacional de cervejaria em igreja.
articles.body:
Entre as notícias que mais chamaram a atenção dos leitores do g1 Zona da Mata nesta semana estão a morte de uma mulher durante um tratamento de canal em um consultório odontológico , a prisão dos irmãos gêmeos integrantes do grupo de pagode Vou Zuar por suspeita de estupro e a conquista de um prêmio internacional por uma cervejaria artesanal instalada no porão de uma igreja .

Relembre três dos destaques publicados entre os dias 14 e 20 de novembro:

Morte durante tratamento de canal em consultório odontológico

Consultório odontológico - foto ilustrativa — Foto: Freepik

Uma mulher identificada como Valéria Siqueira da Silva morreu durante um tratamento de canal em um consultório odontológico de Barbacena , no Campo das Vertentes. O caso foi registrado pela Polícia Militar no sábado (14). A Polícia Civil instaurou um inquérito para apurar as circunstâncias da morte e aguarda o laudo para saber a causa do óbito.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, a paciente passou mal na fase final do procedimento odontológico , apresentou dificuldade para respirar e não resistiu, apesar das tentativas de socorro.

A cirurgiã-dentista responsável pelo procedimento informou à polícia que, antes do início do tratamento, foi realizada a anamnese, etapa destinada ao levantamento do histórico clínico do paciente.

Ainda segundo a dentista, durante todo o atendimento a paciente permaneceu consciente, respondendo às perguntas feitas pela equipe e demonstrando estar bem. No entanto, já na fase final do procedimento, ela apresentou dificuldade para respirar.

As tentativas de reanimação duraram cerca de 45 minutos, mas a paciente não resistiu .

Gêmeos de banda de pagode presos suspeitos de estupro

Irmãos Bruno e Thiago Paiva foram presos por suspeita de estupro em Barbacena — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Os irmãos gêmeos Bruno Paiva e Thiago Paiva, de 36 anos, integrantes do grupo de pagode Vou Zuar, foram presos suspeitos de estuprar uma mulher de 30 anos após um show no sábado (14), na cidade mineira de Barbacena, no Campo das Vertentes.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, a vítima disse que foi ao evento de pagode acompanhada de uma amiga. Após o fim da apresentação, ela teria conversado com um dos integrantes da banda, que a chamou para ir ao camarim. Em seguida, as duas foram de van até um bar com ele e outras pessoas.

A vítima disse que ingeriu bebida alcoólica e que chegou a perder a consciência . Quando ela acordou, segundo o registro, ela estava em um hotel com os dois suspeitos praticando atos sexuais contra ela . A vítima disse que pediu para que eles parassem e, em seguida, deixou o local.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, durante o atendimento, foram identificados vermelhidão no rosto compatível com uso de força; arranhões e escoriações em diferentes partes do corpo; e lesões e inchaço na região íntima.

Após a prisão dos irmãos Bruno e Thiago Paiva, outros dois integrantes do grupo Vou Zuar anunciaram carreira solo . Vitor Naegele informou que seguirá carreira como cantor, enquanto Carlos Vieira passará a atuar como sócio do projeto.

Cervejaria em porão de igreja leva ouro em prêmio internacional

Irmão Taylor mostra cerveja produzida em porão de igreja de Juiz de Fora — Foto: Luiza Sudré/g1

A cervejaria artesanal Hofbauer, mantida há mais de 130 anos por religiosos no porão da Igreja Nossa Senhora da Glória, em Juiz de Fora , conquistou medalha de ouro em competição internacional pelo segundo ano consecutivo . A bebida Alphonsus Maibock recebeu 94 pontos no Brazilian International Beer Awards (BBA) 2026 , realizado em Alagoinhas, na Bahia.

A conquista foi uma das quatro premiações recebidas por duas cervejarias da cidade na terceira edição do concurso , realizada entre os dias 1º e 8 de novembro. Além da Hofbauer, a Buona Cerva também subiu ao pódio, com três medalhas: ouro, prata e bronze.

As duas marcas integram a União das Cervejarias de Juiz de Fora (Unicerva), que reúne produtores locais e reforça a presença do município no cenário cervejeiro mineiro.

articles.title: Casal descobre câncer no mesmo dia e lança livro sobre superação | G1
articles.standfirst: Metade do que for arrecadado com as vendas do livro será doado. Os dois descobriram a doença cerca de um mês antes de passar mil noites em uma viagem de cruzeiro.
articles.summary: Luciana e Claudio descobriram a doença antes de uma viagem e lançam o livro "A Pausa que Mudou o Mundo", com parte das vendas revertida para pesquisas sobre o câncer.
articles.body:
A médica Luciana Paiva e o publicitário Claudio Gomes transformaram o que seria um documentário sobre os bastidores de viagens de navio em um livro sobre superação e cura.

Depois de fazer um "check-up" da própria saúde cerca de um mês antes de passar mil noites em uma viagem de cruzeiro, os dois descobriram, no mesmo dia, que tinham câncer. Luciana estava com câncer no rim. Cláudio, no intestino.

"Foi muito difícil saber que tinha, falar para ele que ele tinha e, ao mesmo tempo, ter que dar a força e falar: 'Nós vamos sair dessa'", relata Luciana.

Intitulada de "A Pausa que Mudou o Mundo", a obra conta desde a experiência do casal por viagens até o choque, o tratamento e a recuperação da doença que fez os dois terem que "recalcular a rota".

Metade do que for arrecadado com as vendas do livro será doado. A maior parte, 35%, será destinada a instituições dedicadas à pesquisa e ao tratamento do câncer, enquanto que os outros 15% vão para projetos de preservação de uma das grandes paixões do casal: o mar.

"O livro não é doença, o livro é vida", diz Claudio.

Luciana fez uma cirurgia e, atualmente, está curada. O companheiro dela ainda trata a metástase com injeções mensais, mas sabe que o pior já passou.

Claudio e Luciana são casados e moram em Ponta Grossa — Foto: RPC

articles.title: Gabriel Félix: influenciador de Uberaba sonhava em ser ator | G1
articles.standfirst: Influenciador fez cursos de modelo na cidade do Triângulo Mineiro, conseguiu trabalhos em São Paulo e sonhava em ser ator. Gabriel morreu aos 29 anos antes de jogar futebol em encontro com amigos em Campinas na quinta-feira (19).
articles.summary: Conheça a história de Gabriel Félix, o influenciador de Uberaba que superou a perda do pai na infância para construir uma carreira de sucesso e uma família aos 29 anos.
articles.body:
A trajetória de Gabriel Augusto Mateus Félix, influenciador que morreu aos 29 anos, começou em Uberaba , no Triângulo Mineiro, onde deu os primeiros passos na carreira de modelo. Entre cursos, trabalhos em São Paulo e planos de se tornar ator, ele construiu uma trajetória em busca dos próprios sonhos. Nesse caminho, conheceu a noiva, Isabelle Abreu, conhecida como Xsbel, com quem formou uma família.

Foi em Uberaba que Gabriel começou a se preparar para trabalhar diante das câmeras. Segundo a prima Gisele Mateus Gonçalves, ele fez cursos de modelo e, depois, conseguiu oportunidades profissionais em São Paulo, onde morou por um período.

“Ele começou a investir na carreira de modelo, fez cursos em Uberaba e foi quando teve trabalhos em São Paulo e ficou uma época lá. Nesse tempo foi quando ele conheceu a Bel, e passaram a ter um relacionamento”, afirmou.

Gabriel conheceu Isabelle pela internet, em 2020, por intermédio de um amigo. Na época, ele morava em Uberaba, enquanto ela vivia no Ceará. Os dois começaram a conversar durante o isolamento social e se encontraram pessoalmente pela primeira vez em 2021, em São Paulo.

“Ele sempre correu atrás dos sonhos dele e, no meio do caminho, ele e a Bel se encontraram”, relembrou Gisele.

Gabriel Fé — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Além da vida a dois, Gabriel e Isabelle também construíram uma trajetória juntos nas redes sociais. Com vídeos de humor, referências à cultura nordestina, moda vintage e registros da rotina familiar, conquistaram milhões de seguidores.

Há mais de três anos, o casal deixou Uberaba e se mudou para Campinas, no interior de São Paulo. A família também costumava viajar ao Ceará, onde vivem os parentes de Isabelle.

A viagem mais recente ao Ceará foi de férias. Ao voltar à rotina, Gabriel planejava construir uma casa em Campinas. Em abril, o casal anunciou a compra de um terreno para realizar o projeto.

O casamento também fazia parte dos planos do casal. Gabriel pediu Isabelle em casamento durante uma viagem à Itália, em 2025. Os dois tiveram uma filha, Amelie, em 2023.

“Eles estavam com casamento marcado, construindo casa e com um futuro gigante pela frente que foi tomado”, lamentou Gisele.

Morte de Gabriel Félix foi anunciada no Instagram — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Lembranças de infância e sonhos de cinema

Em uma homenagem, a prima Júlia Mateus de Freitas Machado também relembrou a infância de Gabriel em Uberaba. Ela o descreveu como uma criança doce, cheia de vida, que transformava os encontros familiares em momentos de brincadeiras, risadas e bagunça.

Entre as lembranças, Júlia citou as brincadeiras na árvore da tia Maria, as disputas para ver quem chegava mais alto, os jogos de cartinhas e as partidas de cobra-cega.

Segundo Júlia, Gabriel também sonhava em ser ator de cinema e dizia que queria um dia estrear nas telonas. A prima destacou ainda a dedicação dele aos projetos profissionais e à família, especialmente à filha.

"Quantas vezes me contou que queria ser ator de cinema, que um dia faria um filme e que nós estaríamos lá, assistindo a você nas telonas. Falava dos seus planos, dos seus sonhos e de tudo aquilo que ainda queria conquistar. Era dedicado, tinha ambições e acreditava no que desejava construir. Seus sonhos eram grandes, assim como você", publicou Júlia nas redes sociais.

Gabriel perdeu o pai ainda criança. Na homenagem, Júlia relembrou que ele queria ser um pai presente e carinhoso para Amelie e proporcionar à filha experiências e momentos que não teve a oportunidade de viver ao lado do próprio pai.

“Você queria proporcionar à sua filha todo o amor, a presença e os momentos que a vida não lhe permitiu viver com o seu próprio pai. E isso diz muito sobre o homem e o pai que você era e desejava ser”

O casal tem uma filha de 3 anos e estava noivo — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Gabriel morreu na noite de quinta-feira (19), após sofrer um mal súbito durante um encontro com amigos para jogar futebo l, em Campinas, onde morava com a noiva e a filha. Ele não chegou a participar da partida, mas passou mal e caiu. Amigos acionaram o atendimento de emergência, mas ele não resistiu.

A causa do mal súbito ainda não foi esclarecida.

O corpo do influenciador será levado para Uberaba, onde será sepultado. Até a publicação desta matéria, a família ainda aguardava a liberação e não havia confirmado o horário da despedida.

A mãe de Gabriel estava em Campinas quando ele morreu. Segundo Gisele, ela ajudava o filho e a noiva nos cuidados com Amelie.

A morte do influenciador deixou familiares e amigos abalados. Na homenagem, Júlia pediu que a história de Gabriel seja lembrada não apenas pela partida precoce, mas pelos sonhos, pelo amor e pelas lembranças que construiui

“Porque pessoas como você não vão embora por inteiro: permanecem nas lembranças, nos ensinamentos e no amor que deixaram”, escreveu.

Gabriel Félix será velado em Uberaba, sua cidade natal — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

articles.title: Macaé Empreendedora amplia conexões, capacitação e negócios a partir do dia 17 | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação gratuita reúne rodadas de negócios, capacitações e atrações culturais em diversos pontos do município.
articles.summary: Programação gratuita reúne rodadas de negócios, capacitações e atrações culturais em diversos pontos do município.
articles.body:
Quarta edição do evento acontece de 17 a 21 de novembro — Foto: Arquivo Secom

A Prefeitura de Macaé e o Sebrae realizam, entre os dias 17 e 21 de novembro, a quarta edição da Semana Macaé Empreendedora. A iniciativa, inteiramente gratuita, percorre diferentes regiões do município com o objetivo de fortalecer o ecossistema de negócios local, fomentar a geração de renda e ampliar redes de parcerias por meio de oficinas, debates, consultorias e ações culturais.

A abertura oficial está marcada para o dia 17, às 17h, no Aeroporto de Macaé. Na ocasião, a partir das 18h, haverá a divulgação de oportunidades vinculadas aos editais Petrobras Cultural. Em seguida, às 18h30, entra em cena a Rodada de Parcerias direcionada a iniciativas de Economia Criativa, Economia Azul e Economia do Esporte, promovendo a aproximação direta entre proponentes e potenciais patrocinadores e investidores.

Na sequência, a programação chega a entidades e polos comerciais do município. No dia 18, a Associação Comercial e Industrial de Macaé (Acim), no Calçadão da Rua Rui Barbosa, sedia pela manhã uma oficina prática voltada à emissão e ao esclarecimento de dúvidas sobre a Nota Fiscal Eletrônica. À noite, o Painel Macaé Empreendedora reúne empresários da cidade para a troca de vivências profissionais, seguido por um debate conduzido pela Associação Macaense de Contabilistas (Amacon) e pelo Conselho Regional de Contabilidade (CRC) acerca dos impactos da Reforma Tributária e das discussões sobre a escala de trabalho 6x1.

As ações do dia 19 atendem a públicos variados e avançam para a região serrana. Enquanto o projeto Conexão Juventude nas Escolas aborda projeto de vida e empreendedorismo com estudantes em Córrego do Ouro, o Shopping Plaza Macaé concentra debates sobre liderança feminina por meio da Sessão de Negócios Sebrae Delas, apresentação do Fundo de Aval para as Micro e Pequenas Empresas (Fampe) e painéis temáticos.

No mesmo dia, o Polo de Cultura Maguinho, em Glicério, recebe palestra do Sebrae sobre o uso de inteligência artificial aplicada à gestão empresarial, acompanhada de intervenção cultural.

No dia 20, as atividades sobem para o distrito do Sana, no espaço CriaSana, com foco em gestão financeira, acesso a linhas de crédito, panorama tributário e mostra cultural. O encerramento ocorre nos dias 20 e 21 de novembro, na Praia de Imbetiba, onde a Secretaria Municipal de Políticas de Promoção da Igualdade Racial (Sempir) promove a tradicional Feira Multicultural Saberes e Sabores, com plantão integrado de atendimento da Casa do Empreendedor para orientar formalizações e tirar dúvidas dos cidadãos.

A Semana Macaé Empreendedora conta com a parceria da Associação Comercial e Industrial de Macaé (Acim), Câmara de Dirigentes Lojistas de Macaé (CDL), Associação Macaense de Contabilistas (Amacon), Zurich Airport Brasil, Aeroporto de Macaé, Macaé Convention & Visitors Bureau e Shopping Plaza Macaé.

Inscrições: Gratuitas e realizadas previamente pelos canais oficiais de cadastro do evento.

Locais de atendimento e atividades: Aeroporto de Macaé, sede da Acim (Centro), Shopping Plaza Macaé, Córrego do Ouro, Polo Cultural Maguinho (Glicério), Espaço CriaSana (Sana) e orla da Praia de Imbetiba.

articles.title: Lavanderia funcional começa pelo planejamento   | G1
articles.standfirst: Piso, parede, bancada e circulação precisam trabalhar juntos em um ambiente compacto, mas de uso intenso.
articles.summary: Piso, parede, bancada e circulação precisam trabalhar juntos em um ambiente compacto, mas de uso intenso.
articles.body:
A lavanderia costuma ficar para uma das últimas etapas da reforma, mas é justamente o tamanho reduzido que torna cada decisão mais importante. Máquina de lavar, tanque, bancada, produtos de limpeza e circulação disputam poucos metros, enquanto água, umidade e uso frequente exigem materiais fáceis de manter.

Antes de escolher os acabamentos, vale começar pela rotina. Onde a máquina ficará? Quanto espaço a porta precisa para abrir? É necessário tanque? Haverá bancada para apoio? Onde ficarão vassouras, baldes e produtos? Essas respostas ajudam a organizar o espaço antes que instalações e revestimentos estejam definidos.

Comece pelas medidas que não podem mudar

Máquina de lavar, tanque e bancada determinam boa parte da distribuição. Além das dimensões dos equipamentos, é preciso considerar pontos de água e esgoto, tomadas e espaço suficiente para circulação e manuseio.

Em lavanderias estreitas, alguns centímetros podem fazer diferença. Uma bancada muito profunda pode comprometer a passagem, enquanto um tanque maior do que a necessidade real pode retirar uma área que seria útil para apoio ou armazenamento.

Medidas dos equipamentos e definição dos pontos hidráulicos ajudam a organizar a lavanderia antes da escolha dos acabamentos — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Paredes precisam acompanhar uma rotina de limpeza frequente

Áreas próximas ao tanque e à máquina estão sujeitas a respingos e pedem superfícies práticas para o dia a dia. O revestimento pode facilitar a manutenção e, ao mesmo tempo, contribuir para deixar visualmente mais organizada uma área que reúne muitos elementos.

O revestimento Originale Bianco 32x60, da Biancogres , é um revestimento de parede branco, acetinado e retificado. A base clara pode funcionar como uma superfície neutra para lavanderias e se relacionar com diferentes cores de bancada, armários e equipamentos.

O Originale Bianco, da Biancogres, cria uma base clara para as paredes e facilita a combinação com bancada, equipamentos e outros elementos da lavanderia — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

No piso, a análise precisa considerar as características indicadas para áreas sujeitas à água e o local de aplicação definido pelo fabricante. Facilidade de limpeza, quantidade de juntas e relação com o revestimento das paredes também entram na decisão.

O metal precisa acompanhar a função da lavanderia

A torneira é outro item que merece ser escolhido a partir da rotina. Dependendo da instalação, ela pode atender somente ao tanque ou também participar da ligação com a máquina de lavar.

A torneira de parede para tanque e máquina, da Roca, foi desenvolvida justamente para esse uso e possui direcionador de jato. O modelo permite concentrar uma função importante da lavanderia em uma peça pensada para esse tipo de instalação.

A torneira para tanque e máquina, da Roca, atende às necessidades da área de serviço com uma solução desenvolvida para esse ponto de uso — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

A posição do metal precisa ser definida junto com tanque, máquina e pontos hidráulicos. Fazer essa escolha somente depois da bancada instalada pode limitar as opções ou exigir adaptações que poderiam ter sido previstas.

Bancada e circulação precisam trabalhar juntas

Mesmo uma pequena superfície de apoio pode fazer diferença para separar roupas, organizar produtos ou apoiar tarefas do dia a dia. Mas a bancada não deve ser dimensionada isoladamente.

A abertura da máquina, a movimentação diante do tanque e o acesso aos armários precisam continuar livres. Em lavanderias compactas, aproveitar a verticalidade com prateleiras ou armários superiores também pode liberar a área de circulação sem ocupar mais piso.

Essa lógica ajuda a evitar um erro comum: tentar colocar todos os recursos possíveis em poucos metros e terminar com uma lavanderia difícil de usar.

Planejar antes evita que a lavanderia vire o espaço que sobrou

Levar para o atendimento da Vilarejo as medidas do local, posição dos pontos hidráulicos e elétricos e dimensões dos equipamentos ajuda consultores e projetistas a analisar revestimentos, metais e distribuição com mais precisão.

Mesmo sendo uma área menor, a lavanderia concentra tarefas frequentes e precisa responder bem à rotina. Quando piso, paredes, bancada, tanque e circulação são definidos em conjunto, o espaço deixa de ser apenas uma área técnica e passa a funcionar de maneira muito mais organizada no dia a dia.

articles.title: Ciclone e frente fria podem provocar temporais no Sul; veja previsão | G1
articles.standfirst: Fim de semana deve ser marcado por temporais, granizo e rajadas de vento que podem superar 80 km/h no Sul. No Sudeste e Centro-Oeste, calor e umidade favorecem novas pancadas de chuva.
articles.summary: Sudeste e Centro-Oeste também devem ter chuva forte no fim de semana. No Sul, há previsão de granizo e rajadas de vento acima de 80 km/h no domingo (22).
articles.body:
Tempestade em Foz do Iguaçu nesta sexta (20). — Foto: Emilson Fernandes

Uma frente fria e um ciclone extratropical próximo ao Rio Grande do Sul podem provocar novas tempestades no Sul do Brasil neste fim de semana.

Há risco de granizo e rajadas de vento. As instabilidades devem ganhar força no domingo (22). No Sudeste e no Centro-Oeste, também há possibilidade de chuva forte.

Segundo a Climatempo, o tempo deve continuar instável neste sábado (21), mas o risco de temporais pode aumentar novamente no domingo, principalmente em áreas do Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina e Paraná.

No estado gaúcho, as rajadas de vento podem superar 80 km/h, com possibilidade de granizo de grande tamanho em alguns pontos. As chuvas também podem atingir áreas da Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre.

Segundo o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia ( Inmet ), uma área de baixa pressão entre o norte da Argentina e o oeste do Paraguai deve continuar transportando calor e umidade em direção ao Centro-Sul do país.

A atuação de cavados atmosféricos, regiões alongadas de baixa pressão, também favorece a formação de nuvens carregadas.

“Nessa época do ano, há muita circulação de umidade, o que favorece pancadas de chuva que podem ser fortes, principalmente à tarde e à noite”, explica César Soares, meteorologista da Climatempo.

Apesar das instabilidades, o calor deve continuar predominando em grande parte do Brasil, inclusive no Sul, com temperaturas próximas ou superiores aos 30°C em várias cidades durante o fim de semana.

Neste sábado (21), a previsão indica continuidade das pancadas de chuva nos três estados do Sul, mas com períodos de sol e calor durante o dia.

No Rio Grande do Sul, os temporais devem ocorrer principalmente no Noroeste e no Norte, sobretudo entre a tarde e a noite. Há possibilidade de granizo e rajadas de vento que podem ultrapassar 80 km/h.

Em Santa Catarina, a chuva deve ganhar força no Norte e em áreas do Vale do Itajaí. No Paraná, os maiores volumes são esperados no Sul, Oeste e Noroeste, também com risco de temporais.

No território gaúcho, os maiores riscos estão no Noroeste, Norte, Nordeste, Serra, Litoral Norte e Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre.

No Sudeste, o fim de semana deve ser marcado por calor, sensação de abafamento e pancadas de chuva, que podem ganhar força durante a tarde e a noite.

Em São Paulo, há previsão de pancadas moderadas a fortes nos dois dias, com possibilidade de raios, rajadas de vento e granizo.

No sábado, o maior risco de temporais deve se concentrar no Sul e no Centro do estado.

Já no domingo, as chuvas mais intensas podem atingir principalmente o Norte e o Nordeste paulista.

Em Minas Gerais, a chuva deve continuar volumosa em áreas do Noroeste e do Vale do Jequitinhonha durante o sábado, enquanto o Leste do estado tende a registrar redução das precipitações.

No Espírito Santo, a tendência é de diminuição gradual da chuva ao longo do fim de semana, mas ainda há possibilidade de pancadas isoladas.

No Rio de Janeiro, o tempo deve continuar quente e instável, com períodos de sol entre nuvens e risco de chuva forte.

Apesar da passagem da frente fria, não há previsão de queda significativa das temperaturas no Sudeste.

Mapa mostra previsão de chuva para este sábado (21/11) em todo o Brasil. — Foto: CPTEC/Inpe

No Centro-Oeste, a combinação de calor e umidade deve continuar favorecendo pancadas de chuva em Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Goiás e no Distrito Federal.

No sábado, as instabilidades devem aumentar principalmente no Centro-Norte de Goiás e em áreas de Mato Grosso.
